prompt: Give a byte stream message boundaries: write a Content-Length header before each body, and read back exactly that many bytes over a loopback socket. Complete sendFramed and readFramed.
explanation: TCP delivers a stream of bytes with no notion of where one message stops, so every real protocol adds framing -- here a Content-Length header followed by a blank line. The header must be read one byte at a time: a BufferedReader would happily pull in part of the next message and lose it forever. Reading the body needs a loop too, because InputStream.read can legally return fewer bytes than you asked for, and the length is measured in UTF-8 bytes rather than characters, which is why multi-byte text is the interesting test case.
hints: body.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8).length is the number you put in the header -- body.length() would be wrong for any non-ASCII character.
Read the header with single in.read() calls, appending each byte as a char to a StringBuilder, and stop when the text endsWith("\r\n\r\n").
Fill the body array with a loop: int read = in.read(body, filled, length - filled); add read to filled until filled == length, and treat a -1 as an early end of stream.
